channel.title: Smithsonian / USGS Weekly Volcanic Activity Report
channel.description: The Weekly Volcanic Activity Report is a cooperative project between the Smithsonian's Global Volcanism Program and the US Geological Survey's Volcano Hazards Program. Updated by 2300 UTC every Thursday, these notices are preliminary and subject to change as events are studied in more detail. This is not a comprehensive list of eruptions during the week, but rather a summary of activity that meet selected criteria. Carefully reviewed, detailed reports are published in the Bulletin of the Global Volcanism Network.

item.title: Krakatau (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported an increase in low-level eruptive activity at Krakatau starting in early October. During 21 September-9 October seismicity indicating both shallow and deep magmatic processes did not significantly increase. Minor white-to-black ash plumes were occasionally visible in webcam images rising as high as 50 m above the crater, though weather conditions sometimes prevented views. Satellite data indicated low sulfur dioxide emissions as high as 238 tons per day and low-level thermal anomalies. Five eruptive events were recorded during 6-8 October, followed by nine eruptive events just on 9 October, indicating increasing low-level activity. The Alert Level was raised to 3 (on a scale of 1-4) at 2100 on 9 October and the public was advised to stay 5 km away from summit.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Manam (Papua New Guinea) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC) reported that ash plumes from Manam rose to 2.1 km (7,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifted E, NE, N, and NW during 8-9 and 11-13 October.

Source: Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC)

item.title: Marapi (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Marapi (on Sumatra) continued during 8-14 October. An eruptive event was recorded at 0002 on 13 October by the seismic network but not visually observed due to weather conditions. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 3 km away from the active crater.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Nevados de Chillan (Chile) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - New Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (SERNAGEOMIN) and the Servicio Geológico Minero Argentino (SEGEMAR) reported that eruptive activity at Nevados de Chillán was ongoing in mid-October. A new lava flow was first visible at the summit of Nuevo volcano on 29 September and traveled SW. During a field visit on 1 October scientists observed the ejection of meter-sized blocks as high as 500 m above the summit and outward as far as 250 m. The blocks landed on the flanks and rolled up to 400 m from the crater rim. During 8-14 October activity was characterized by periodic long-period earthquakes indicating fluid movement at depth, and occasional ash plumes and explosions. Weather conditions sometimes prevented views. At 1655 on 8 October an ash plume rose 860 m above the summit and drifted SE. A long-period earthquake was detected at 0330 on 12 October and was associated with the ejection of incandescent material onto the upper flanks. At 1224 on 12 October an ash plume rose 500 m and drifted SSE. A series of consecutive explosions around midday on 13 October produced ash plumes that rose as high as 600 m above the summit, with the tallest plume recorded at 1354. A long-period earthquake was detected at 1548 on 13 October along with an acoustic signal indicating explosive activity; weather conditions prevented visual confirmation. An ash plume rose 400 m at 1558 on 14 October. A few hours later, at 1957, another seismic signal indicated explosive activity. The Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-color scale) and the public was warned that an eruption may impact areas within 2 km of the active crater. The Sistema y Servicio Nacional de Prevención y Repuesta Ante Desastres (SENAPRED) maintained an ?Preventive Early Alert? for Pinto and Coihueco and warned the public to stay 2 km away from Emission Center 3 (EC3).

Sources: Servicio Geológico Minero Argentino (SEGEMAR),Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (SERNAGEOMIN),Sistema y Servicio Nacional de Prevención y Repuesta Ante Desastres (SENAPRED)

item.title: Aira (Japan) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Minamidake Crater (Aira Caldera?s Sakurajima volcano) during 5-12 October. Crater incandescence was visible in nighttime webcam images during 5-9 October. A total of 15 eruptive events during 5-8 October produced ash plumes that rose 1-1.6 km above the crater and drifted in various directions. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a 5-level scale), and the public was warned to be cautious within 1 km of both the Minimadake and Showa craters.

Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

item.title: Bezymianny (Russia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported that effusive activity at Bezymianny continued during 8-14 October. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on most days; the volcano was occasionally obscured by weather clouds. Dates and times are provided in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC); events are in local time only where specified.

Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)

item.title: Dukono (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that eruptive activity at Dukono continued during 8-14 October, though hazy conditions prevented visual observations. Eruptive events were recorded by the seismic network during 8 and 10-12 October. Faint rumbling was heard at the Dukono observation post (11 km N) on 10 October. The Alert Level remained at Level 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 4 km away from the Malupang Warirang Crater.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Etna (Italy) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported that eruptive activity at Etna?s summit craters during 5-11 October was characterized by gas emissions at the summit craters and periodic minor ash emissions at Northeast Crater (NEC). Adverse weather conditions often prevented visual observations. The volcano Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) according to the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile.

Sources: Dipartimento della Protezione Civile,Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV)

item.title: Fuego (Guatemala) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Instituto Nacional de Sismología, Vulcanologia, Meteorologia e Hidrología (INSIVUMEH) reported that eruptive activity at Fuego continued during 6-14 October. Daily explosions recorded by the seismic network, at rates of 2-8 per hour, generated gas-and-ash plumes that rose as high as 1.1 km above the summit and mainly drifted as far as 40 km in various directions. Shock waves and rumbling sounds from explosions were reported almost daily. Explosions also often ejected incandescent material, sometimes as high as 300 m above the summit, and onto the flanks causing incandescent block avalanches; notable avalanches descended the Seca (W), Taniluyá (SSW), Ceniza (SSW), Honda, and Las Lajas (SE) drainages, sometimes reaching vegetated areas. On 7 October lahars descended the Mineral and Seca drainages, carrying tree branches, trunks, and blocks as large as 3 m in diameter. Ashfall was reported in El Porvenir (11 km SW), El Rodeo (10 km SSE), La Reina, La Reunión (7 km SE), and surrounding areas during 6-7 October, in Yepocapa (8 km NW) and nearby areas during 10-11 October, and in Panimaché II (8 km SW), Yepocapa, and surrounding areas during 13-14 October.

Source: Instituto Nacional de Sismologia, Vulcanologia, Meteorologia, e Hidrologia (INSIVUMEH)

item.title: Great Sitkin (United States) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO) reported that slow lava effusion continued to feed a thick flow in Great Sitkin?s summit crater that advanced SE during 7-14 October based on webcam and satellite images. Minor earthquakes consistent with the growth of the lava dome and occasional rockfalls were detected by the seismic network. Weather clouds obscured webcam and satellite views during most of the week, though elevated surface temperatures were identified in satellite images during 7-8 October. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Watch (the third level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the third color on a four-color scale).

Source: US Geological Survey Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO)

item.title: Ibu (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Ibu continued during 1-7 October, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Daily gray or white-to-gray ash plumes rose 200-800 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the public was advised to stay 2 km away from the active crater and 3.5 km away from the N crater wall opening.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Kanlaon (Philippines) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported continuing eruptive activity at Kanlaon during 7-14 October. The seismic network recorded 0-19 daily volcanic earthquakes and during 11-13 October 5-6 daily periods of volcanic tremor lasting 2-64 minutes. In general, sulfur dioxide emissions ranged from 932 to 3,219 tonnes per day (t/d), though a peak of 4,656 t/d was recorded on 10 October, the same day as a larger eruptive event. Moderate-to-voluminous volcanic emissions generally rose as high as 1.2 km above the summit and drifted in various directions. A moderately explosive eruption at 1246 on 10 October produced an ash plume that rose 5-6 km above the summit and drifted NNE. The event lasted for two minutes, though ash emissions were recorded for two hours and 41 minutes. The Office of Civil Defense - Negros Island Region (OCD-NIR) reported that residents of Bago City observed the ash plume, heard booming sounds, and felt the ground shake. A sulfur odor was reported in parts of barangay Codcod in San Carlos City. Ashfall and a sulfur odor were reported in barangay Ara-al, Gintubdan, and in the barangays Igmayaan, Bunga, Bacong, Kumaliskis, Bago, and Pandanon, in Don Salvador Benedicto, based also on a news report. Residents of La Carlota City heard rumbling. On 11 October a total of 10 ash emissions lasting 11 minutes to three hours and 33 minutes generated ash plumes that rose as high as 600 m above the summit and drifted NNW, NW, and W. Several of the events were visible in webcam images; at 0318 minor Strombolian activity produced an ash plume that rose 500 m above the summit and drifted WNW. At 0000 and during 0545-0724 on 12 October ash plumes rose 300 m above the crater rim and drifted NW. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 0-5); the public was warned to stay out of the 4-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) and pilots were advised to avoid flying close to the summit.

Sources: Inquirer.net,Office of Civil Defense, Republic of the Philippines,Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)

item.title: Karangetang (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Karangetang?s North Crater (Kawah Dua) continued during 8-14 October. White plumes rose as high as 20 m above the summit and drifted in various directions on most days. At 1402 on 11 October a white-and-gray ash plume rose 700 m above the summit and drifted W and NW. Nearly an hour later, at 1459, a white, gray, and brown ash plume rose 700 m above the summit and drifted W and NW. Faint rumbling was heard on 12 October, though no emissions were recorded. Incandescent avalanches on the flanks were visible in a 13 October webcam image. Dense white plumes rose as high as 1 km above the summit an drifted N and NW on 14 October. A 5 October new article noted that lava flows or incandescent avalanches of material descended the flanks 700 m S, as far as 1 km SW and W, and 100-700 m NW. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was advised to stay 1.5 km away from both craters, with an extension to 2.5 km on the NW and SW flanks of North Crater.

Sources: Antara News,Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Kilauea (United States) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by incandescence, intermittent spatter, and lava flows from vents along the SW and W margins of Halema`um`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 7-14 October. Incandescence and flaming continued to be visible at the N and S vents during 6-11 October, with periodic spattering at the N vent. Robust volcanic gas plumes rose from both vents in daytime webcam views. Several small lava overflows from a small vent at the base of N vent were observed during 9-10 October. The small vent also intermittently spattered until 2315 on 10 October when it began continuously effusing a small, tube-fed pahoehoe flow. Overnight during 11-12 October moderate-to-strong incandescence was visible at the N vent, at the vent near its base, and at the S vent, while incandescence from the W vent fluctuated, with visibility potentially affected by fog. Intermittent flames and minor spattering associated with gas jetting occurred at all vents, including a short period of sustained spattering at the S vent that began at around 0318 on 12 October. Spattering from the vent at the base of the N vent occurred intermittently. Visible spattering ended at around 0635. Vigorous dome fountaining began at the N vent just before 1130 on 13 October, lasted nearly an hour, and produced a lava flow that traveled about 1 km. This was the longest and most vigorous dome fountain since 30 September. Two other substantial fountain and overflow episodes occurred at 1600-1640 and at 1700-1720. Interspersed between and following these longer events were about 15 smaller events that lasted only a few minutes and produced flows less than 100 m long. Sustained fountaining was followed by gas jetting, often with sprays of spatter produced during drainbacks of lava within the vents. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Watch (the second highest level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code at Orange (the second highest color on a four-color scale).

Source: US Geological Survey Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO)

item.title: Lewotolok (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported continuing eruptive activity at Lewotolok during 8-14 October. On 8 and 11 October dense gray ash plumes rose around 500 m above the summit and drifted W and NW, and white steam-and-gas plumes rose 100 m above the summit and also drifted W and NW on 9, 12, and 14 October; no emissions were recorded on 10 and 13 October. Active lava flows on the S and SE flanks were 400-600 m long. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4). The public was warned to stay 2 km away from the summit with an extension to 3 km on the S and SE flanks.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Masaya (Nicaragua) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that on 9 October ash plumes from Masaya were visible in webcam images rising to 1.2-1.5 km (4,000-5,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifting SW and W. Weather clouds blocked satellite views.

Source: Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)

item.title: Mayon (Philippines) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Mayon during 7-14 October. The seismic network recorded 6-14 daily volcanic earthquakes. Sulfur dioxide emissions generally averaged 905-1,474 tonnes per day. Daily emissions rose 100-900 m above the crater and drifted WNW, WSW, and SW. Minor Strombolian activity at 0318 on 11 October generated an ash plume that rose 500 m above the summit and drifted WNW. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a 0-5 scale) and the public was reminded to stay away from the 6-km-radius Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ). PHIVOLCS recommended that civil aviation authorities advise pilots to avoid flying close to the summit.

Source: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS)

item.title: Merapi (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Merapi (on Java) continued during 8-14 October with avalanches produced by the active lava dome on the upper SW flank. The seismic network recorded multiple lava avalanches per day on most days that traveled as far as 2 km down the Sat/Putih, Bebeng, and Krasak drainages on the SW flank and the Boyong drainage on the S flank. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4), and the public was warned to stay 3-7 km away from the summit, based on location.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Popocatepetl (Mexico) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Centro Nacional de Prevención de Desastres (CENAPRED) reported that eruptive activity was low at Popocatépetl during 7-14 October. The seismic network recorded 19-42 long-period events per day, accompanied by steam-and-gas emissions that drifted in multiple directions; the emissions contained small amounts of ash on a few of the days. The seismic network also detected one volcano-tectonic earthquake per day on 9, 11, and 13 October. According to the Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) ash plumes were visible in webcam and satellite images during 12-14 October rising 6.1-7.3 km (20,000-24,000 ft) a.s.l. (as high as 1.9 km above the summit) and drifted W and WSW. The Alert Level remained at Yellow, Phase Two (the middle level on a three-color scale) and the public was warned to stay 12 km away from the crater.

Sources: Centro Nacional de Prevencion de Desastres (CENAPRED),Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)

item.title: Purace (Colombia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC) reported that during 8-14 October daily ash plumes from Puracé rose to 5.1-6.1 km (17,000-20,000 ft) a.s.l., or as high as 1.4 km above the summit, and drifted NW, WNW, and SW based on webcam images, satellite images, weather models, and Volcano Observatory Notices to Aviation issued by the Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC). Emissions on 13 October were considered likely, but were not detected due to weather conditions. The Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-color scale).

Source: Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC)

item.title: Sabancaya (Peru) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Instituto Geofísico del Perú?s (IGP) Centro Vulcanológico Nacional (CENVUL) reported continuing eruptive activity at Sabancaya during 5-11 October. The seismic network detected 18 seismic events associated with the movement of magmatic fluids, along with earthquakes indicating internal rock fracturing; no volcanic explosions occurred during the period. Gas, steam, and ash emissions periodically rose as high as 800 m above the summit and drifted less than 10 km NE and E. Moderate sulfur dioxide emissions averaged 865 tons per day, and 12 thermal anomalies (each 1 MW or less) associated with the lava dome were identified. The Alert Level remained at Orange (the third level on a four-color scale) and the public was warned to stay outside of a 12 km radius from the summit.

Source: Instituto Geofísico del Perú (IGP)

item.title: Santa Maria (Guatemala) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Instituto Nacional de Sismología, Vulcanología, Meteorología e Hidrología (INSIVUMEH) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Santa Maria?s Santiaguito dome complex during 7-14 October, with continuing lava extrusion at Caliente dome. Incandescence at the summit was observed during dark hours. Effusion of blocky lava and collapses of material produced daily incandescent block avalanches that descended the flanks, particularly the W, SW, and S flanks; during 7-8 and 11-12 October these collapses generated short pyroclastic flows that reached the base on the cone. Daily explosions, 0-3 per hour when reported, generated gas-and-ash plumes that rose as high as 1.1 km above the dome and drifted SW and W. On 7 October lahars descended the Nimá 1 drainage on the SW flank and the Tambor drainage on the SSW flank, carrying sediment, tree trunks, branches, and volcanic blocks up to 1 m in diameter. Ashfall was reported in Santa María de Jesús (5 km SE), the villages of Belén (10 km S) and Calaguache (9 km S), and other nearby communities during 7-8 October, in La Trinidad (13 km SSE), Santa Nita, Nueva Destina, Pawilonia, Rosario, and San Marcos Palajunoj (8 km SW) areas during 12-13 October, and in the mountainous area of the Monteclaro settlement and its surroundings during 13-14 October.

Source: Instituto Nacional de Sismologia, Vulcanologia, Meteorologia, e Hidrologia (INSIVUMEH)

item.title: Semeru (Indonesia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity continued at Semeru during 8-14 October, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. White-to-gray or gray ash plumes rose 300-1,000 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions on most days; emissions were not visible due to weather conditions on 8 and 10 October. The Alert Level remained at 3 (the second highest level on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay at least 5 km away from the Jonggring Saloko Crater in all directions, 13 km from the summit on the SE flank along the Kobokan drainage, and 500 m from the banks of the Kobokan drainage as far as 17 km SE of the summit.

Source: Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG, also known as CVGHM)

item.title: Sheveluch (Russia) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported continuing lava effusion and explosive activity at the lava domes along the N crater floor of Young Sheveluch (on the SW flank of Old Sheveluch) during 7-14 October. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on a few of the days; weather clouds occasionally obscured views. The Aviation Color Code remained at Orange (the second highest level on a four-color scale). Dates are based on UTC; specific events are in local time where noted.

Source: Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT)

item.title: Stromboli (Italy) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV) reported that eruptive activity continued at Stromboli during 5-11 October. Webcam images showed Strombolian activity from vents in Area N within the upper part of the Sciara del Fuoco, and vents in Area C-S (South-Central Crater) on the crater terrace. Explosions at Area N ejected lapilli and bombs above the vents and explosions at Area C-S ejected both fine and coarse tephra above the vents. The daily frequency of explosions at both vents was at medium level and the intensity of the explosions was generally at low levels. Lava overflowed vent N1 in Area N at 1505 on 5 October and ended at 0050 on 6 October. The lava flow descended the upper part of the Sciara del Fuoco. A second overflow occurred later that morning during approximately 0925-1040. The Alert Level remained at Yellow (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) according to the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile.

Sources: Dipartimento della Protezione Civile,Sezione di Catania - Osservatorio Etneo (INGV)

item.title: Suwanosejima (Japan) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that eruptive activity at Suwanosejima's Ontake Crater during 7-8 October produced ash plumes that rose as high as 400 m above the crater rim. The activity was the first recorded since 25 July. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second level on a five-level scale) and the public was warned to be cautious within 1.5 km of the crater.

Source: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA)

item.title: Taal (Philippines) - Report for 8 October-14 October 2026 - Continuing Eruptive Activity
item.description:
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported eruptive activity at Taal during 6-12 October. The seismic network recorded 0-34 daily volcanic earthquakes, including 1-9 periods of volcanic tremor each day during 7-10 October, with periods lasting between 2 and 82 minutes. Daily gas-and-steam emissions generally rose 600-1,500 m above the crater rim and drifted W, SW, and SE. Sulfur dioxide emissions averaged 952-3,071 tonnes per day during 6 and 8-10 October. A minor phreatomagmatic eruption at 1806 on 8 October generated a dark ash plume that rose 4 km above the crater rim and drifted SW. Incandescent material and lightning were visible in the plume. The event lasted for five minutes based on seismic data and webcam footage. According to a news source at least 120 people, or 32 families, evacuated to centers as of 1053 on 9 October. The Alert Level remained at 1 (on a scale of 0-5); PHIVOLCS reminded the public that the entire Taal Volcano Island (TVI) was a Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) and recommended that the Main Crater and areas along the Daang Kastila fissure should remain prohibited. Pilots were warned to avoid flying over TVI.

Sources: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) ,Philstar News
